title: Scalar tensor of a completion output is complete
statement: For a prime l, finite extensions E and F of Q_l with a specified Q_l-algebra embedding i : E → F, a scheme W with no geometric restrictions, and K in the actual completed-coefficient ambient derived category for E [lem-pbc-scalar-tensor-construction], scalar tensor of the canonical source completion reflection of K [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] is intrinsically complete for the target coefficient datum. This asserts only completeness of this particular object, not a comparison of completion functors or any unit equation.

source.place: Tags 099B and 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; the concrete finite-free scalar argument of lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-completion-transport, steps 2--3 (agent specialization).

proof.text: Transport the coefficient map, fixed by all residue projections, through pbcCompletedComparison. Finite freeness of the integer extension gives the finite-free basis of the actual completed coefficient sheaf by the continuous-section and quotient-limit construction.

The source completion output is intrinsically complete by reflection. Apply the finite-free coordinate argument: after scalar restriction its scalar tensor is a finite direct sum of this output, hence source-complete. Exact scalar restriction detects completeness for the image of the source parameter. That parameter is a unit times a positive power of the target uniformizer; the unit-power criterion identifies this with target completeness. Transport through the intrinsic Cech/Koszul presentation comparison. Zero objects and the empty scheme satisfy the same reflection and finite-sum argument.
